title: The night watchman's tally

data.source: Gaussian streams with a step change, 4000 streams per setting.

prediction: If CRR's cut were the CUSUM alarm, the delay after a change would not depend on when the change comes. Predicted instead: CUSUM's delay stays flat, while the R2 cut gets slower the later the change, because it measures the rise from the last cut and CUSUM measures the rise from the lowest point since.
baseline: Page's CUSUM (1954), the standard change detector, optimal in the worst case (Lorden 1971; Moustakides 1986).
why: The equivalence does not hold. CUSUM is a first passage above the running minimum; the R2 cut is a first passage above the last cut. After a long quiet spell that one difference made the cut many times slower than CUSUM.
